ce_bugs.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — For a destination calendar row with a null credentialId the fan-out calls createEvent without an externalId while GoogleCalendarService resolves the target by credentialId match, so the event lands in "primary" and the reference records externalCalendarId undefined - a write that "succeeds" into the wrong calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credentials are fetched by raw id from the DB with no ownership or app-enabled check, bypassing getApps validation used in the constructor, so a destination calendar pointing at another user's or a globally disabled app's credential is still used to write events.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — On merge (newBookingId) only the first old calendar reference is deleted via `.find`, so the other hosts' old calendar events are orphaned after reschedule-into-existing-booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1067 — BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED payloads emit `destinationCalendar: null` while cancel/reject/payment paths now emit `[]`, so the same public field is inconsistently null vs empty array across triggers.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose destinationCalendar is null/[] throws a TypeError

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all COLLECTIVE host calendars when the event type and organizer have no destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — createEvent matches destination calendars by credentialId, so legacy destination calendars with a null credentialId no longer match and the event is silently created on "primary" instead of the configured calendar

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is tautologically unreachable (it only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy), so calendarId becomes undefined instead of the destination calendar id

packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — credential` is declared once outside the per-reference loop, so if a reference's credential lookup fails the stale credential from the previous iteration is used to update that calendar

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — createEvent still always uses destinationCalendar[0], so with multiple destinations every host's event is written against the first host's calendar id (same issue at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:452 — recurring cancellation still picks only the first `_calendar` reference per updated booking, so the extra host calendar events created by this feature are left behind
packages/core/EventManager.ts:598 — when the error is thrown before calendarReference is assigned the catch now returns an empty array instead of a failed EventResult, hiding the failure from callers
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:757 — the new loadUsers catch rewrites every error to 400/500, so an HttpError thrown inside loses its original status code and message context

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Dead branch: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same dead branch as updateEvent — the `find` on `externalCalendarId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always yields undefined and silently falls back to "primary".

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-cancel block was moved inside the new per-reference loop but does not use `reference`, so the credentials x updatedBookings deleteEvent fan-out is repeated once per calendar reference (N x C x B redundant external deletes)

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:126 — CalDAV `createEvent` is now invoked once per destination but always resolves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (index 0), so each extra host adds a redundant `listCalendars()` DAV round-trip plus a duplicate write to the same calendar

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Office365 `createEvent` ignores the new `credentialId` argument and always targets the first destination's externalId, so N-1 of the N per-host calls are wasted duplicate writes to the same calendar

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — Destinations without a `credentialId` fan out to every credential of that integration type once per destination, so multiple such destinations multiply calendar API inserts

packages/core/EventManager.ts:369 — When no credential is found in memory or in the DB for a destination calendar, the host is silently skipped with no log and no failure EventResult, so the booking reports success while that host's calendar was never written.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Video booking references no longer persist `credentialId` (was `result.credentialId`), so handleCancelBooking.ts:491 skips deleteMeeting and cancelled bookings leave their video room live and joinable.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credential is loaded by raw id from the DB with no userId/teamId or host-membership check, so any credentialId reachable via a DestinationCalendar row is used to write calendar events, bypassing the previous `this.calendarCredentials` ownership scoping.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Same unscoped `prisma.credential.findUnique` fallback on the update path: a BookingReference.credentialId now drives use of an arbitrary user's calendar credential without an ownership check.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — No test covers destinationCalendar being an empty array, yet `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining and six call sites now emit `[]` (e.g. confirm.handler.ts:175, webhook.ts:119).

mrv_findings.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` dereferences `.integration` on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` with no optional chaining, so any booking whose `destinationCalendar` array is empty (the documented "no calendar" sentinel used everywhere else in this diff) and whose location is Google Meet throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video — the exact "no Google Cal" case this line exists to handle is the case that crashes it; confidence 100, severity P0.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:78-86 vs packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1254,1676,2002 — `constructor(user: EventManagerUser)` builds `this.calendarCredentials` solely from the single `user.credentials` passed in (`new EventManager({ ...organizerUser, credentials })`), so for a COLLECTIVE booking `event.destinationCalendar[]` now legitimately contains other hosts' `credentialId`s that can never be found in `this.calendarCredentials`, meaning the new prisma-fallback branch isn't a rare cache-miss path but the mandatory path for every non-organizer host on every booking; the real fix (scope EventManager to all hosts' credentials) was skipped in favor of a per-item DB patch; confidence 100, severity P0.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-374 and :511-541 — inside `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` (and the analogous `for (const reference of calendarReference)` at update time) the code does `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId }, ... })` per iteration with no batching, an N+1 query pattern that (per the finding above) fires for every additional host on every booking create/update rather than being an edge case, and could be replaced by a single `findMany({ where: { id: { in: [...] } } })` before the loop; confidence 100, severity P1.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423,433-441 — `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) { ... const foundCalendarCredential = await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }); ...}` repeats the same sequential per-reference DB lookup pattern for every calendar reference on cancel, again scaling linearly with host count with no batching; confidence 100, severity P1.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:356-368 and :529-541 — `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) { credential = { appName: credentialFromDB?.app.slug ?? "", id: ..., type: ..., key: ..., userId: ..., teamId: ..., invalid: ..., appId: ... }; }` silently leaves `credential` undefined (skipping calendar-event creation/update for that host with no log or surfaced error) whenever the credential's linked app record is missing a slug, and this hand-rolled reconstruction bypasses the `getApps()` normalization/enablement pipeline used to build every other entry in `this.calendarCredentials`, creating two divergent, driftable ways of producing a "credential" object; confidence 75, severity P2.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 — `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null,` uses `null` for the "no calendar" sentinel while every other producer touched in this diff (webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts:251-254/531-534, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts, bookingReminder.ts) uses `[]` for the identical semantic state, so downstream consumers that assume one sentinel over the other diverge in behavior depending on which code path produced the event; confidence 100, severity P1.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (the exact sentinel set two lines earlier when the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar), so a COLLECTIVE booking where team members do have personal destination calendars but the organizer does not will silently drop all of those hosts' calendars — the specific "collective multiple host" scenario this task claims to fix; confidence 90, severity P0.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-383 — `createAllCalendarEvents` iterates every element of `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(...)` for each with no deduplication by `credentialId`, so nothing in the type or the loop prevents two array entries from carrying the same `credentialId` (or from being backed by the same underlying credential), which would create the same calendar event twice for that credential; confidence 50, severity P2.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>;` makes `credentialId` a required part of the `Calendar` interface contract, but `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72` (`async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent): Promise<NewCalendarEventType> {`) and `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125` (same signature) were never updated and still pick `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (array index 0) regardless of which credential is actually creating the event — only `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:87,100-124` was fixed to select the destination matching the passed `credentialId`; TypeScript's fewer-parameters compatibility rule lets this compile silently, so for Office365/Lark every non-first host in a collective booking gets its event written against the wrong destination calendar entry, defeating the task's stated goal for two of the three calendar integrations in this repo; confidence 100, severity P0.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 and packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1074 — `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null;` is added to the shared `CalendarEvent` interface and set via `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType,`, but no code in this repo reads `evt.schedulingType`/`calEvent.schedulingType` anywhere (the one consumer that needed it, the collective-calendar push at handleNewBooking.ts:1077, reads the already-in-scope local `eventType.schedulingType` instead), making it redundant derived data bolted onto a widely shared/serialized type with zero enforced sync guarantee and no current consumer; confidence 100, severity P3.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` dereferences the destructured element without a `?.`, so any Google Meet booking whose `destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/`[]` (handleNewBooking:1063 returns `null`, every other builder returns `[]`) throws TypeError and the booking 500s (conf 100, P0).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar), so the task's core case — collective hosts' calendars — is dropped with no warning (conf 90, P1).
